evidence.text: The entry states that 住 is not recorded in Shuowen. Although the page lists categories for oracle-bone, bronze, and other historical-form references, those images are not publicly available there. It therefore supports a gap in accessible early graphic evidence, not a claim that 住 was absent from those scripts.

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: The entry analyzes 住 as 从人、主聲 and gives ‘stop’ as the basic sense. It cites the Guangyun gloss 住，止也, a Jin-period example from Pan Yue for stopping, examples for staying, and separate residence examples. It also lists 住 as used through 駐 for stationing troops. This is a dictionary synthesis of usages; the cited examples do not establish the graph’s formation date.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 漢語多功能字庫, Chinese University of Hong Kong
evidence.text: For 住, the entry displays modern Mandarin zhù and two Guangyun fanqie entries, 持遇 and 中句, associated with distinct Middle Chinese initial categories 澄 and 知. The page does not supply a same-system historical reading for 主 in this entry, so these categories alone do not establish a historical sound comparison.
evidence.title: 漢語多功能字庫

evidence.source: 汪維輝, 漢語詞彙史漫談
evidence.field: 住的早期用例與語義變化
evidence.text: The author identifies a Western Han passage in Jia Yi’s 新書 as an early ‘stay/remain’ use and a line in 靈樞經 as another early example, while cautioning that the latter text’s dating is uncertain. The account places frequent ‘stop/remain/stand’ uses in Eastern Han Buddhist translations and traces residence uses from late Han–Three Kingdoms texts, becoming dominant by the Eastern Jin 法顯傳. These are literary-text attestations reported by a modern secondary study, not securely dated manuscript attestations; its proposed semantic path is stop/remain or stand → stay/lodge → reside.
evidence.title: 汉语词汇史漫谈 | 汪维辉：古代人如何“居住”

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart 2014, local exact row cross-check
evidence.text: The inspected local Baxter–Sagart 2014 row for 主 gives Mandarin zhǔ, MC tsyuX, OC *toʔ, gloss ‘master; host’. This is the component’s reading in this reconstruction system; compare the separately recorded row for 住. A local row is dataset evidence, not proof of a phonetic role.
evidence.title: Baxter-Sagart Old Chinese reconstruction, version 1.1 (20 September 2014)

evidence.source: Baxter and Sagart 2014, local exact row cross-check
evidence.text: The inspected local Baxter–Sagart 2014 row for 住 gives Mandarin zhù, MC drjuH, OC *dro(ʔ)-s, gloss ‘stop (v.)’, GSR 0129g. Compared within Baxter–Sagart’s system, this differs from 主 zhǔ, MC tsyuX, OC *toʔ. The similarity provides a possible phonetic relationship but does not independently date the graph or prove a specific sound change.

gaps: No dated oracle-bone, bronze, or excavated manuscript form of 住 was verified. The Ministry of Education dictionary says 住 is absent from Shuowen but its historical-form image references were unavailable. No graphic change sequence or corruption proposal is supported by the inspected sources.

The earliest proposed ‘remain/stop’ examples come from transmitted Western Han and early medical texts; their manuscript transmission and dating do not establish a securely dated earliest graph attestation. The reported shifts toward residence are based on textual usage analysis, not a dated artifact sequence.

The source word for the independently depicted referent of 主 remains unsettled here. That uncertainty does not by itself invalidate 主 as a sound component within 住; 主 and 住 have separately recorded readings in the Baxter–Sagart 2014 system, with distinct but potentially compatible Old Chinese forms.
The supplied exact local Baxter–Sagart rows were inspected for both 主 and 住. The published PDF open failed, so the linked external page could not be checked directly in this run.
Official Unihan pages for both characters returned browser internal errors. Exact local kMandarin rows establish 主 zhǔ and 住 zhù as local data only; no upstream page content is asserted.

The proposed historical glyph candidate is a modern vector redraw of a Shuowen seal-script form of 主, not an artifact image and not a historical form of 住. The exact Commons description establishes its stated identity and public-domain release, but the direct original image open failed; it is supplied as a candidate for the phonetic component only. No actual early glyph image of 住 was established.
